> *"China has made progress in the following six fronts: employment, financial sector, foreign trade, basic living needs, food and energy security, and expectations."*

- This statement combines elements of the "six fronts" (employment, financial sector, foreign trade, foreign investment, domestic investment, and expectations) with elements (basic living needs, food and energy security) from the "six key areas."
- The six key areas are a **distinct set** from the six fronts, and **basic living needs** is one of the six key areas, not the six fronts.

> *"China has increased its GDP volume by 30 trillion yuan over the past five years, and the 14th Five-Year Plan is the first five years in which China has became a modern socialist country in all respects."*

- The 2021 report states that GDP increased from **less than 70 trillion yuan to over 100 trillion yuan** over the five-year period of the 13th Five-Year Plan. This implies a **30 trillion yuan increase**, so this part is **correct**.
- However, it also states that the **14th Five-Year Plan** represents the **first five years of embarking on a new journey to build China into a modern socialist country**, not that it has **already become** one.
- Therefore, the second part **overstates** the status and is **incorrect**.
